"El hermano perdido de Metal Slug":

He aquí, y gracias a Dotemu por portearlo, otro gran juego de los arcade, que al igual que con los "Metal Slug", obtenemos una experiencia frenética, con muchos balazos, explosiones y un tumulto de posibilidades por explotar. 

- Campaña: Grupos de soldados encaminándose a vencer a una organización terrorista con planes de dominación mundial... algo trillado, pero de todas maneras, solo existe para complementar al juego. 
Esta posee 3 caminos diferentes, con posibilidad de alternar de ruta luego del stage 3. Cada ruta posee sus caminos, formación de enemigos determinada, y pese a que algunos jefes son algo derivativos entre sí (quizás un poco más de diferencias según el escenario elegido no hubiera sentado mal), no deja de ser un buen desafío y hasta satisfactorio sobrevivir a ello. 


- Gameplay: la base es que hay un botón para disparar, cruceta o palanca para movimiento y dirección, evasión y lanzamiento de bomba. Lo interesante de este aspecto, es que tenemos 8 personajes a elegir, tanto en modo solitario como en equipo, cada personaje tiene sus contrastes entre sí, aciertos, defectos y cambios en la velocidad de movimiento según el escenario abordado. Por ejemplo, uno es versátil en exteriores, pero puede moverse un poco más lento en fábricas, como otro lo hace al revés, lo cual, sumado al desafío, le da muchísima rejugabilidad, incluso para experimentar.

En cuanto al botón del disparo, si lo presionas cerca de un enemigo, puede soltar un objeto, para puntaje o un power up, este mismo punto ya abre muchas posibilidades para atacar constantemente cuerpo a cuerpo, como el posible drop del arma "Hyper", la mejor arma del juego.


El jugador posee una barra de vida, recuperable con comida/medicinas que aparecen durante el trayecto y matando con melé a los enemigos (incluso, algunos minijefes/jefes sueltan una medicia grande cuando mueren así, así que se recomienda golpearlos cuando brillen de rojo).


- Personajes: no serán complejos, pero igual poseen cierto encanto por ser muy diferentes, hasta con voces, animaciones propias, e imagen propia durante el cutscene final del juego, al terminarlo con cada uno.
(Like al Maru por vender completos) :D 


- Música: En general, funciona y "Ride on", que suena al principio del juego, me parece un track memorable y épico.

- Comparaciones con Metal Slug: Sé que algunos hacen esta comparativa, por poseer algunas similitudes, como el ser un Run n Gun con temática militar, matando tumultos por montón, hasta a mí me recuerda al otro juego. Sin embargo, están lejos de ser lo mismo, aparte de que ST salió justo un año después de MS. tienen sus diferencias cruciales, Por lo que me cuesta pensar que este se inspiró en el otro.


Concluyendo, estamos frente a otro excelente juego de arcade que los demás deben probar, incluso los fans de Metal Slug. Y por mi parte, estoy anhelando a que surja un nuevo juego indie que tenga a ST como referente :D .

[h1]¿Porque le dicen Big Mama?, pues... porque es una madrezota, ósea una madre grandota.[/h1]
Síganme para más traducciones chingonas.

Que bonitos años donde lo simplicidad era norma y no se sobre explicaba nada; eres un wey mamado o mona chichona con metralleta que va a matar a un terrorista y ya, lo demás no interesa.

[h2]>A Grandes Rasgos:[/h2]
Pues... esta obrita, es ya un título retro de la época del Metal Slug, y el "auge" de las arcadias (90s tardíos), como su secuela, era de las mieles que uno podía obtener al ir por las tortillas y quedarse el cambio, pues era casi obligado que los locales tuvieran alguna arcade y un catálogo de opciones, aunque siempre fui más de Metal Slug, si llegué a ver este título y su secuela en estos locales, sin jugarlos en ese entonces.

Dicho lo anterior, y como siempre digo; se valora el esfuerzo de preservar obras, aunque a veces no sale tan... bien, en esta ocasión al menos puedes terminar el jueguito y es funcional en Win11, solo hay que mover el escalado en propiedades; de 100% para abajo debería de servir. 

[h3]>En Sumario:[/h3]
+Un "Run n gun/Sidescroller" arcade divertido, y bastante detallado para la época.
+Tiene un rooster variado de personajes; dejando de lado los protas; wey mamado/mona chichona, hay personajes de donde escoger y si varia su ataque secundario y hitbox.
+La banda sonora es buena, las melodías de SNK tienen su encanto.
+Un título fácil de agarrar para una tarde en los que no se pretende hacer mucho.
-No esperes tanta longevidad en un arcade: 40 minutos exagerado en 5 stages, aunque hay 3 caminos a seguir y sus variantes por run.
-No es de los mejores trabajos de Dotemu, aunque se agradece el esfuerzo.

[h2]Concluyendo:[/h2]
Pues... como esfuerzo de preservación es pasable 6/10, al menos comparándolo con su segunda parte, que como mencione en aquella reseña; no es terminable aquel, el presente caso si viene bien el jueguito aunque con fallos con la relación de aspecto al menos en win11, quitando eso, a estas alturas ya es cultura digital de los videojueguitos y pues tiene ese encanto de tiempos más simples, aunado a que llega a costar menos de un dólar 7/10.

Террористическая группировка под названием "Кровавые скорпионы" похитила ученого и его внучку и заставила ученого разработать новый вид наркотика, который сделает любого человека намного сильнее, чем это возможно. Мир не может допустить, чтобы это произошло, поэтому специальная команда , условно назавём их "коммандос" отправилась на задание, чтобы помешать Кровавым скорпионам захватить власть в мире.

На выбор предлагается в общей сложности 8 различных солдат. У каждого персонажа есть свое особое оружие или бомба, и все персонажи обладают разными характеристиками. Однако разница не так уж велика, поэтому лучше выбирать солдата по внешнему виду. Каждый раз, когда вы начинаете новую жизнь, вы можете выбирать между двумя режимами: "Одинокий волк" и "Командный бой". В "Одиноком волке" вы играете за одного солдата, но в "Командном бою" вы можете переключаться между 3 разными персонажами. Однако, поскольку у этих трех персонажей одинаковое количество очков здоровья, я предпочитаю играть за Одинокого волка, поскольку выбор трех персонажей занимает больше времени, чем одного.

Игровой процесс в этой игре очень похож на Metal Slug и другие игры Run and Gun, однако в этой игре есть одно большое отличие. Вид в этой игре похож на игры Legend of Zelda, и вместо прыжков вы можете перекатываться, чтобы уклоняться от вражеских пуль. Вы можете выбрать 3 разных пути, чтобы добраться до шестого и заключительного этапа, так что, возможно, вам захочется пройти его как минимум 3 раза, даже если финал будет одинаковым.

Ракурс в этой игре немного отличается от таких игр, как Metal Slug и Contra, но это также делает ее не такой увлекательной, как в этих играх. Мне также очень не хватает возможности прыгать. Может быть, и забавно потратить на Shock Troopers одну-две жизни и несколько минут, но я никому не рекомендую тратить на эту игру слишком много времени, а то надоест.

雖然說是1997年的街機遊戲，但是有一個特點放在當時可以說是非常前衛。

[b]「這款街機遊戲有迴避無敵啊！」[/b]
那個年代的射擊遊戲說真的沒幾款有迴避功能的，更別說迴避時間為無敵狀態，光這點就很讓人值得一玩了。

[b]「這款街機遊戲還有多重路線啊！」[/b]
是的，這款遊戲並非線性關卡，雖然在當年有些街機遊戲本身就有兩種路線，但這款遊戲是「初始給你三個路線作為選擇」，以這點來說還是挺前衛的。

[b]●遊戲時間[/b]: 30~50分鐘 (依路線而異)
[b]●遊戲難度[/b]: 難度較高，具有難度選擇機制
[b]●續命機制[/b]: 可以設定為無線續命可以放心通關，另外還有20次續命以及10次續命讓玩家挑戰自己的極限

雖然這款俯瞰視角遊戲放在現代，那個射擊方式真的可以說是特別反人類，但撇除這點來看其實這款遊戲是相當優秀的作品，如果你想體驗那一個年代的懷舊魅力的話那麼請務必購入試試看。

Shock Troopers, developed by SNK Corporation and Dotemu and published by SNK Corporation, is a high-octane top-down shooter that captures the intensity and energy of classic arcade gaming while showcasing the unique personality that defined SNK’s golden age. Originally released in 1997 for the Neo Geo MVS and later revived on Steam, the game stands as one of the best examples of the run-and-gun formula done with speed, flair, and replayability in mind. Unlike its side-scrolling contemporaries, Shock Troopers gives players complete directional freedom, letting them move and shoot across expansive battlefields teeming with enemies, explosions, and chaos. It’s a game that thrives on movement and aggression, rewarding both quick reflexes and strategic thinking in equal measure.

The premise is pure arcade simplicity. A terrorist organization has kidnapped a scientist and his granddaughter, and a team of elite commandos is sent to rescue them. From the very start, Shock Troopers sets itself apart through choice. You can play solo as a “Lonely Wolf,” selecting one character to carry through the entire mission, or choose “Team Battle” mode, which allows you to assemble a squad of three soldiers that can be switched between during gameplay. Each of the eight selectable characters has distinct attributes—some are faster, others are stronger, some excel at defense or wield more powerful special attacks. This variety gives the game a surprising degree of depth for its genre, letting players experiment with different team compositions and tactics. Add to that a branching level system that allows you to choose between multiple routes (Mountain, Jungle, or Valley) and you get a game designed for replayability long before such a concept became a staple of modern design.

What truly makes Shock Troopers stand out is its sense of control and pacing. The player is not limited to linear paths or fixed directions; you can move in eight directions, roll to evade enemy fire, and unleash powerful special weapons when situations get dire. The controls are fluid, allowing for a constant rhythm of movement, attack, and evasion that feels both fast and responsive. Enemies swarm from every angle, forcing you to stay in motion, and the ability to roll or strafe adds a layer of dynamism rarely seen in shooters of its era. This fluidity transforms every stage into a ballet of bullets and explosions, where skill and spatial awareness are constantly tested. Boss battles punctuate each stage with grand spectacle—massive tanks, helicopters, and mecha-like war machines fill the screen with firepower, demanding quick reflexes and precision dodging.

Visually, the game remains a feast of late-90s arcade art direction. The pixel work is exceptionally detailed, with vibrant backgrounds and destructible environments that make the battlefield feel alive. Explosions bloom across the screen in bursts of color, enemy vehicles burst into flames, and small environmental details—like enemies carrying away wounded comrades—add surprising personality. The attention to visual feedback makes every hit satisfying, and the chaos never becomes unreadable thanks to SNK’s excellent use of color contrast and motion clarity. Complementing this is an energetic soundtrack filled with electric guitar riffs and fast-paced percussion that perfectly matches the rhythm of battle. The sound effects—gunfire, explosions, and character grunts—maintain the kinetic energy of the gameplay and enhance the adrenaline rush that defines the experience.

The Steam version, brought to life by Dotemu, preserves the essence of the arcade original while adding a few modern conveniences. Features like save states, customizable controls, and online leaderboards allow both newcomers and veterans to experience the game in different ways. Unfortunately, the port is not without its issues. Some players have reported minor sound glitches, input lag, and emulation inconsistencies, which can slightly detract from the crispness of the original. These technical imperfections don’t ruin the experience but do serve as reminders that this is still an emulated version of a game designed for a different era. Despite these flaws, the gameplay remains as addictive and satisfying as ever, proving that good design transcends hardware limitations.

From a design perspective, Shock Troopers’ replay value is one of its strongest assets. The branching path system encourages multiple playthroughs, as each route presents unique environments, enemies, and boss encounters. The ability to choose between single-character or team-based playstyles adds another layer of strategy, especially for players looking to master the game’s mechanics. The scoring system rewards aggressive play and precision, appealing to the competitive spirit that defines arcade gaming. While it lacks the humor and spectacle of SNK’s other famous run-and-gun series, Metal Slug, it compensates with smoother gameplay, faster pacing, and a greater emphasis on player choice. The difference is tonal—where Metal Slug embraces chaos and slapstick violence, Shock Troopers is more focused and militaristic, offering a more tactical flavor of arcade action.

Even with its age, Shock Troopers remains remarkably accessible and enjoyable. Its gameplay loop is instantly understandable—move, shoot, dodge, survive—but it leaves plenty of room for mastery. It captures a level of purity and immediacy that few modern shooters can replicate. Every enemy killed, every explosion dodged, and every level cleared feels earned through reflex and focus. The game doesn’t rely on story or progression systems to keep you engaged; it hooks you purely through the satisfaction of play. This is what made SNK’s arcade games so enduring—their ability to deliver tight, replayable experiences where every run feels like an opportunity to improve.

In the end, Shock Troopers stands as one of the hidden gems of the arcade era and one of SNK’s finest non-fighting game achievements. It’s a reminder of how much depth and excitement can be packed into a game built on straightforward mechanics and skill-based gameplay. Despite minor technical flaws in its Steam version, the core experience remains electrifying—fast, fluid, and endlessly replayable. For anyone who loves the intensity of old-school action, the precision of tight controls, and the joy of mastering challenging levels, Shock Troopers offers a timeless and exhilarating ride through the heart of classic arcade warfare.

Rating: 8/10

[h2]Об игре:[/h2]
 - [b]Shock Troopers[/b] — это типичный аркадный Run'n'Gun со всеми вытекающими из этого нюансами вроде кучи врагов разной степени толстоты и расцветки и одноклеточных боссов, занимающих львиную часть экрана.(Так что да,нахрапом игру не пройти)

Hungry for more arcade games, my friend and I settled on Shock Troopers - another SNK game, essentially being a top down Metal Slug. Would it reach the highs I craved, or was it attempting to fill a void it couldn't possibly aspire to?

The story of this game is as basic an affair as you'd expect. Somebody gets kidnapped, you go to rescue them. The game actually has very basic cutscenes reminiscent of Ninja Gaiden, which feel like they're mostly there to show off the superb pixel art.

The controls of this game are surprisingly intuitive. You can move and fire in 8 directions, but holding the fire button lets you strafe. You can also activate/throw a special weapon depending on your character (but it has limited ammo, so use it wisely!), and you can dodge roll (this will become your best friend). When starting the game, you pick your character (or team if you want to play as three characters you switch between) and a route. Each character has a different speed, type of gun, and of course animations.

But, more ambitiously, the routes are almost completely different to one another. While bosses are sometimes shared, the level design and environments are completely different from one another. There's also a point midway through the campaign where you can actually hop from one of the three routes to another – making the game feel very replayable (I would know, my friend and I already played it twice thanks to an unfortunate glitch where the audio just stopped working...)

The cat's out of the bag at this point, I loved this game. It's brutally difficult – the amount of bullets you'll be dodging and the speed of some bosses towards the end would have consumed a great deal of my quarters were I an (American) kid, but the combat is just really, really fun. Working with a friend to split the enemies apart and round em up, frantically dodging through and between bullets, all while some genuinely great music plays in the background, it's euphoric.

I'm honestly a little sad there's only two entries in this series (to my knowledge) as I enjoyed this so much I want to look forward to much more of it.

Shock Troopers is another game from the NeoGeo era, it was one of those Arcade Machines that nobody would come close to and they had that mysterious aura about them... Renown for being extremely difficult, even on Easy Difficulty.

That was then, when we'd literally crawl on the side of the pavement looking for coins that we can input into the Arcades and play... Now that we've had the blessing of UNLIMITED CREDITS, the game seems to suddenly be a tad more forgiving.

In Shock Troopers, you choose one of eight characters, with each having their own special stats. For example, "That Blonde Dude" is slow as hell, but he's got a lot of Health Points, while that "Scrawny Blonde Girl" has higher movement speed, but all it takes for her to die are two bullets. Another difference between the characters would be their "Side Weapon"; ranging from grenades to literal Rocket Launchers. The level design is pretty nice; you can choose one of three paths and the campaign is six missions long (just like Metal Slug). Some paths are easier but we're not going to discuss that! The graphics are amazingly done in glorious retro style pixel art... and it would make you quite intrigued to know that most objects in the level are entirely destructible. That's right, your gun can unleash a mayhem so vast you'd be glued to your screen trying to satisfy your OCD by leaving NOTHING standing. Each mission has a boss at the end of it, but they're usually the same tank with a different color swap and when you destroy it, a cringe boss-looking soldier jumps out of it to try their luck lol.

The plot includes some girl getting kidnapped that has ties with the president of the USA or something... Sorry, I was too invested in the killing and destruction to actually care. Shock Troopers gets a whooping [b]9.5/10[/b]. It's an almost perfect game in my book... Almost because too much mayhem sometimes causes the game to lag! [b]Shock Troopers[/b] es un juego de disparos vista cenital porteado por DotEmu. Su lanzamiento original fue en 1997 para la Neo Geo. Es considerado como uno de los clásicos destacados del género, y su estilo de juego rápido y frenético se ha mantenido vivo a lo largo de los años.

La premisa del juego es simple pero efectiva: el jugador elige uno de los ocho mercenarios, cada uno con habilidades y armas únicas, y se lanza a través de niveles llenos de enemigos y obstáculos. En el camino es posible encontrar diversas armas y algunos power ups que dan cierta variabilidad. Lamentablemente, su argumento es pobre como los 90 nos tenía acostumbrado, sin embargo su jugabilidad vale completamente la pena. 

La mecánica de juego es sencilla, lo que lo convierte en un juego adecuado tanto para jugadores casuales como para aquellos que buscan algo más desafiante. Los controles son precisos y responsivos, lo que permite a los jugadores moverse con agilidad mientras esquivan balas y explosiones enemigas. No hace abuso de la dificultad y se puede continuar infinitas veces. Es posible jugarlo en cooperativo con hasta un jugador más (y dos latas de cerveza) lo que agrega un plus a la experiencia y el concepto de poder elegir diferentes rutas, dan cierta rejugabilidad.

[b]Shock Troopers[/b] es un juego corto que puede terminar en algo así de 45 minutos. El agregado de logros extiende la vida útil y se puede jugar perfectamente con gamepad. I recommend the Shock Troopers offered here, but just barely.  Because while Shock Troopers is probably my favorite overhead run 'n gun, the port on Steam here is just awful.

This version of Shock Troopers is likely going to be fine for anyone that hasn't played it before.  It might seems a tad buggy, but nothing that prevents playing it. It also might feel a little sluggish, but it also doesn't necessarily require fast reflex inputs either.  And the overall experience is okay.  But as someone that has played Shock Troopers elsewhere, this port just feels off.  

The music doesn't sound quite right.  The lag is noticeable.  And I'm going to have to take a look at my screen settings, because the more I play it, the more it feels like the game is slightly zoomed in from how I remember it.

As for the game itself, you play as one of the many commandos or shock troopers lone wolf, or as a team of them with team play.  Each character is armed with a different secondary weapon like grenades, guided missiles and satchel charges.  The character also has a roll, or duck if on a motorcycle, to avoid damage.  

While shooting the character aims in the direction they are moving while tapping and are locked in that direction if the button is held.  If the character gets close to an enemy, they will perform a melee attack.  This attack dispatches the weakest of enemies, but not all infantry.  The characters have a life bar that depletes everything they are hit.  Though, there are health picks throughout the level and some enemies drop them, too. Shock Troopers offers three paths to get to the main bad guy's base.  Each level have different challenges to deal with and offer some replay value.  The game also has 4 difficulty settings.  However, this is still an arcade style game.  So don't expect to beat it on a single credit your first few play throughs.

The port of Shock Troopers here on Steam isn't very good.  And if there ever is a Neo Geo collection put together by someone competent like M2, I absolutely wouldn't recommend buying this version.  However, short of that, I still find this game tons of fun even with the flawed port here.
